claim.statement: The Walker has no autonomous decisions: it is an interpreter of CognitiveRhythm oscillator signals. 'Selective' halts (rare, n=15) produce dramatically shorter walks (mean 2.33 concepts) than 'exhausted' (mean 15.40) or 'amplitude_death' (mean 11.82) halts, confirming that the oscillator physics — not a Walker decision — determines walk length when the step budget runs out. This sharpens the M.46 F2 finding: at linguistic discontinuities, oscillator physics drove M1/M3/M4 to consume the step budget in 1-3 concepts, NOT a strategic Walker choice to emit one concept.
claim.operationalization: Across 515 cycles, partition by halt_reason and compute mean walk length. Prediction (under oscillator-driven Walker): selective halts << amplitude_death < exhausted, because selective = budget-filled-on-subset is purely a function of how fast the oscillator drove the operators. Verify factor difference > 4× between selective and the other modes.
claim.h0: Walk length is independent of halt_reason (Walker is autonomous)
claim.h1: Walk length is determined by halt_reason via oscillator physics

preregistration.analysis_plan: Partition by halt_reason; compute mean walk length; verify ratio.

verdict.reasoning: selective: mean 2.33 (n=15, range 1-11); exhausted: mean 15.40 (n=146, range 6-25); amplitude_death: mean 11.82 (n=353, range 0-26). Ratio exhausted/selective = 15.40/2.33 = 6.61× (predicted >= 4×). amplitude_death walks are intermediate, confirming M2 fires only AFTER the Walker has done some walking (gamma had to lead AND collapse via Routh-Hurwitz). The selective halt's tiny mean (2.33) demonstrates oscillator-driven Walker: physics consumed the budget on 1-3 concepts. Sharpens M.46 F2 (id c89a128f…): the discontinuity-detector finding is a CONSEQUENCE of oscillator physics, not strategic Walker choice.
